Thank you for your review. Please accept the Practice's sincere apologies if any distress has been caused to you or your family. Please be advised that under GDPR regulations the Practice is obliged to take consent from all Patients over the age of thirteen before speaking with a family member or a representative.  The Patient also has to be present when telephoning the telephone triage line.  When you reach this triage you are entering into a telephone consultation and the Doctor is present, to offer a diagnosis and treatment based on the Patients symptoms.  You would not be able to preempt the questions that may be asked therefore the Patient must present to answer them.  if it is not possible for the Patient to be present with you in person, then a three way telephone call may take place between the caller, the Patient and the Practice.  We have many Patients who do so.  In certain circumstances where a Patient over the age of 13 is very unwell and is not able to be present then a history may be taken from the Parent or representative.  This is only done when it is deemed clinically unsafe not do so at that moment in time.  These are very rare cases as all emergencies would be visiting A&E via an ambulance and not contacting the Practice. Due to an unprecedently high demand in General Practice, once the Receptionist has informed you of the protocol they will have to move on to the next call.  This is to avoid delay in the system.  You, yourself have stated that you "waited in a queue of 23 people ahead".  Other people would also have been waiting in the queue behind you.  The Practice operates a telephone triage  twice a day from Monday to Friday (0900-1000 and 1430-1530).  This is a dedicated service, offered to ensure all Patients receive clinical intervention at the point of call.  They are then signposted for further clinical intervention as required.  You state your wife rang at approximately 4pm and the Practice closes at 6.30pm.  it is not realistic to expect a call back within two and a half hours as staff have workloads they are required to attend to on a daily basis.  Patients are usually called back within two working days, most receiving this call within twenty four hours.  Your wife stated in her message she left for the Practice Manager that she "expects an urgent call back otherwise she would leave a bad google review".  Please be advised this type of threatening behavior is not acceptable.  We cannot operate a safe clinical system in fear of Patient retaliation when the system does not cater to their preference or convenience.  I hope this answers any questions you may have had.
